title: The 10 Best Corded Car Polishers
subtitle: Dual-action and rotary buffers for waxing, swirl removal and paint correction, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A car polisher spreads wax in minutes and, with the right pads and compound, removes swirls and light scratches that hand polishing can't. We ranked 10 best-sellers on rating, review volume and features (dual-action motion, variable speed, a soft start and a 2-year-plus warranty). The type matters most: dual-action (random orbital) polishers are hard to damage paint with and suit beginners; rotary buffers cut faster but can burn paint in inexperienced hands. Simple orbital waxers just apply and buff wax. They run from about $27 for WEN's 6-inch waxer to $220 for Chemical Guys' TORQX kit.

avoid.name: ZOTA Buffer Polisher, 1600W 7 Inch/6 Inch Car Buffers and Polishers Kit, 7 Variable Speeds (P702)
avoid.flag: 13.3 A draw; calls itself rotary and dual action
avoid.verdict: A budget buffer that can't decide what kind of polisher it is. For the same $50, the AOBEN is a real dual-action polisher with 1,711 reviews at 4.5 stars.
reasons: It lists a 13.3 A draw. A standard 15 A household circuit is meant to carry about 12 A continuously, so a long polishing session on a shared garage circuit can trip the breaker. DEWALT's pro rotary draws 12 A.
The listing calls it a 'dual action polisher' while it's sold as a 1,000-3,500 rpm rotary buffer. The difference decides whether it's safe for a beginner on car paint.
At 4.1 stars it's the lowest-rated polisher we compared.

buyers_guide.a: Dual-action (random orbital) polishers oscillate as they spin, so they don't build heat in one spot and are very hard to burn paint with. Rotary buffers spin in a fixed circle, cut faster and remove deeper defects, but they can burn through clear coat in seconds if you hold them still. Beginners should start with a DA.
A simple orbital waxer applies and buffs off wax. It won't remove swirls or scratches. For paint correction you need a DA or rotary with cutting pads and compound.

buyers_guide.q: What speed should I polish at?
buyers_guide.a: Spread product on low speed, then compound at medium-high and finish at medium. Variable speed lets you match the pad and product.
A cutting pad (wool or firm foam) with compound for swirls, a polishing pad with polish to refine, and a soft finishing pad for wax or sealant.

buyers_guide.q: Can I use a polisher on headlights and boats?
buyers_guide.a: Yes. Polishers restore cloudy headlights with the right compound, and rotary buffers are common for oxidized gelcoat on boats.
